# RustyNES v2.9.8 — "Vanguard"

The preparation release for v3.0.0. It carries v3.0.0's planned breaking changes early, fixes the rendering defects found by booting every staged game, brings the game database's corrections to every platform, and adds menu options to the MiSTer core. **Read the breaking changes before upgrading.**

## Breaking changes

v3.0.0's planned breaks landed here, so that v3.0.0 itself can be a tested milestone. v3.0.0's notes will list them again.

- **Older saves are not found for cartridge games.** A game is now identified by the bytes after its header, so a corrected header never loses its saves again. Save states, battery `.sav` files, cheats and movies made with earlier versions are not picked up. FDS and NSF games are unchanged.
- **Save states from v2.9.7 and earlier are refused** with a message saying so, and **movies older than this release are refused** with a message to re-record them.
- **A movie records the console it was made on.** It records the console model, the chip revisions, the power-on state, the Four Score, the Vs. switches and the Game Genie codes. Playback uses them whatever your settings are, and puts your settings back afterwards. Raw RAM cheats are switched off while a movie records or plays, because a movie cannot carry them.
- **Netplay peers must match on these options**, not only on the ROM. A mismatch is refused with the reason, so a session cannot silently drift apart.
- **For developers:**
  - `LockstepBus` is renamed `SystemBus`.
  - The APIs deprecated since v2.7.5 are removed, and so is `serialize_header`.
  - `Header` and `FrameInput` are `#[non_exhaustive]`.
  - Movies keep Four Score players 3 and 4.

## Games that render correctly now

Every one of the 748 staged dumps was booted and its final frame looked at. The games that drew garbage or nothing led to these fixes:

- **The game database no longer overrides a correct NES 2.0 header.** It was running ten games as the wrong board, among them *Youkai Club*, the Sachen *Lightgun 2-in-1*, *Saint Seiya*, the *Magical Taruruuto-kun* games and *Don Doko Don 2*.
- **PAL games in old-style headers run at PAL timing**, using the database's region: *Pin Bot (E)* and *Sidewinder*.
- **Board fixes:** *Megami Tensei II* (Namco 163), *Skull & Crossbones* (RAMBO-1), *Magic Floor*, the *76-in-1* multicart, *Vs. Super Mario Bros.* (work RAM), *Nintendo World Championships 1990*, *Famicom Jump II*'s graphics, the mapper 191 translations, and *Balloon Fight (J)* translated to Russian (a header with junk bytes).
- **Vs. The Goonies** draws in its own palette.
- **The Pulsewave demo** shows its postcard: VRC6 CHR banks now power on in order. That value is a documented assumption.
- 44 dumps for the newest mapper families are now pinned by a baseline and a screenshot each. Mislabelled dumps are recorded rather than forced.

## On every platform

- **Android, iOS and the libretro core now apply the game database's header corrections**, as the desktop and the web build always did.
- **Power Cycle keeps your settings.** Before, it dropped OAM decay, a custom palette, the fast dot path and the audio filter until the next load.
- **A game's settings are applied before its first frame.** On a game-to-game load, the emulator could run a frame first. A late power-on fill then rewrote RAM under the running game.

## On iOS

- **The iOS app builds, launches and plays again.** v2.9.7's Swift did not compile on a Mac. Once it did, it opened to a black screen, and it crashed at launch when built without the iCloud capability. All three are fixed (#578), and CI now compiles the app for every release.

## On the desktop

- **A Famicom console model** (Settings > Emulation > Accuracy), off by default. Its PPU leaves reset before the CPU, which the *999-in-1* multicart depends on.
- **Vs. DualSystem cabinets** start as two consoles from the command line too, and Power Cycle resets the whole cabinet.
- **Toggling "Fast PPU dot path" mid-game no longer wipes work RAM.**
- **Colour emphasis follows the documented NTSC hardware model**, instead of a fixed dim per bit.

## The MiSTer core

New menu options, **compiled and timing-closed but not yet seen on hardware**:

- your two custom aspect ratios from `MiSTer.ini`;
- integer scaling;
- a 224-line vertical crop;
- a choice of the FBX "Smooth" or the 2C03 RGB palette.

The core's colours now match the emulator's, entry for entry, and a new co-simulation gate checks this.

Both builds were re-swept on the new RTL, and fitter seed 2 stays pinned. On-die every seed closes. Off-die, three seeds fail, and seed 2 closes with 33 ps of setup margin, the thinnest this project has pinned.

Both bitstreams are compiled from the release commit at fitter seed 2, on the day of the release, because the build date is part of the design. Two clean compiles of each build were checked byte-identical before the release. The md5 of each attached file is added to this page when the files are attached.

**No hardware has run any bitstream.**

## Performance

- **Removing the dead /NMI edge detector** made a frame 4.9% to 6.1% faster on three of the four benchmark workloads, and 1.4% faster on the fourth. Measured on its own, over two runs.
- **Three small hot-path changes** were adopted from an 11-candidate re-measurement, together 1.8% to 4.3% faster. Their output is byte-identical, so the accuracy is unchanged.
- **Against v2.9.7 as a whole**, the shipped `nestest` frame is about 5% to 9% faster in both runs. On the other workloads the end-to-end gain did not reproduce. Something else in this release appears to offset the two measured gains there, and it is being investigated for v2.9.9 rather than claimed.
- Rejected after measurement, with the numbers recorded in `docs/performance.md`: a palette read-view cache and a struct-layout change.

## Verification

- The full suite, with the test ROMs and every local commercial suite, passes on the release tree: 3,357 tests, 0 failed, 19 ignored. AccuracyCoin is 144/144 and nestest is 0-diff.
- Each fix has a test that failed before it, and reverting the fix makes that test fail again.
- Every changed baseline was looked at and attributed to its cause.
- Co-simulation: on-die 175 passed, 0 failed, 1 expected failure; off-die 176 / 0 / 1.
